question: How can feedback improve a paragraph?
example: A draft says “The system is fast.” A reader needs to know which task became faster and by how much.

nodes.title: 1. Set the criterion
nodes.body: A criterion is a condition for success. Here the claim should name the task and give a measured comparison.

nodes.title: 2. Write a draft
nodes.body: “The search returns sooner.” The draft names a task. The reader still needs a comparison.

nodes.title: 3. Check the draft
nodes.body: Which task got faster? What did we measure? Record the missing evidence before revising.

nodes.title: 4. Prepare a revision
nodes.body: The timing is missing. Find the measurement or remove the claim, then revisit the criterion.

stop: Finish when the draft supports the claim. If time runs out or the evidence is unavailable, report what is missing.
takeaway: The reviewer identifies a specific gap. That finding gives the writer a concrete change to make on the next pass.
limit: The arrows trace a draft that still needs work. A draft that meets the criterion can leave the cycle after review.
